title: Bounded powers in a finite normed field extension give a bounded monic relation
statement:
Let $F$ be a complete field with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, and let $L/F$ be a field extension admitting a finite $F$-basis. Let $
u:L	o\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ be a norm on its underlying $F$-vector space: $
u(x)=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $
u(x+y)\le\max(
u(x),
u(y))$, and $
u(cx)=|c|
u(x)$ for $c\in F$. No multiplicativity of $
u$ is assumed. If $a\in L$ satisfies $\sup_{m\ge0}
u(a^m)<\infty$, then there is a monic polynomial $q(T)=T^e+\sum_{j<e}c_jT^j\in F[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], with $e\ge1$, $|c_j|\le1$ for every $j<e$, and $q(a)=0$.

source.place: Finite-extension norm theorem and its bounded-powers consequence for integral elements of the valuation ring. WANTED: book not available locally; source location is descriptive, not an asserted verified theorem number.

proof.text: The finite $F$-basis of $L$ makes $L$ a finitely generated $F$-module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] with $A=F$ and $B=L$: every $x\in L$ has a monic annihilating polynomial, hence $L/F$ is algebraic. For each $x$ choose a monic annihilator $p_x$ of least degree. Such a polynomial has positive degree, since the only monic constant is $1$, which does not vanish in the field $L$. Two monic least-degree annihilators have the same degree and their difference is a lower-degree annihilator; if that difference were nonzero, dividing it by its leading coefficient would contradict minimality. Thus $p_x$ is the unique monic minimal polynomial. This explains the notation in the spectral-norm input without assuming separability.

source.place: Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral; the choice and uniqueness of a least-degree monic annihilator are the elementary argument written here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension] to this algebraic extension of the complete nontrivially normed nonarchimedean field $F$. It gives the norm $s(x)=\operatorname{spectralValue}(p_x)$, with $s(xy)=s(x)s(y)$, $s(1)=1$ and $s(cx)=|c|s(x)$. We use the given norm $\nu$ only as a vector-space norm; no multiplicativity or submultiplicativity of $\nu$ has been asserted.

proof.text:
Use two copies of the underlying $F$-vector space $L$, with norms $
u$ and $s$. Both are Hausdorff topological $F$-vector spaces: their norm distances separate points, and the strong triangle inequality controls sums of increments, and $N(cx-c_0x_0)\le\max(|c|N(x-x_0),|c-c_0|N(x_0))$ for either norm $N$, with $|c|$ bounded near $c_0$, proves continuity of scalar multiplication; negation preserves the norm. The identity $\iota:(L,
u)	o(L,s)$ is $F$-linear, its source has a finite $F$-basis, and $F$ is complete and nontrivially normed. Hence [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous] makes $\iota$ continuous. Apply [lem-trf-continuous-linear-map-norm-bound] to obtain a single constant $C>0$ with $s(x)\le C
u(x)$ for every $x\in L$.

Choose a real $M\ge1$ with $\nu(a^m)\le M$ for every $m\ge0$, using the bounded-powers hypothesis. Multiplicativity of $s$ and $s(1)=1$ give $s(a^m)=s(a)^m$ by induction, including $m=0$. Therefore $s(a)^m\le CM$ for every $m$. If $s(a)>1$, put $\delta=s(a)-1>0$. Induction gives $(1+\delta)^m\ge1+m\delta$: multiplying the inductive inequality by $1+\delta$ adds the nonnegative term $m\delta^2$. Choose a natural $m>(CM-1)/\delta$ to obtain $s(a)^m\ge1+m\delta>CM$, a contradiction. Thus $s(a)\le1$.

proof.text: Take $q=p_a$ from step 1 and put $e=\deg q\ge1$. The defining identity $s(a)=\operatorname{spectralValue}(q)$ and step 4 give $\operatorname{spectralValue}(q)\le1$. The monic-polynomial criterion [lem-sfb-monic-spectral-value-coefficients] now gives $|q_j|\le1$ for every natural index $j$, in particular for $j<e$. Since $q$ is monic, its coefficient expansion is $q(T)=T^e+\sum_{j<e}q_jT^j$; it satisfies $q(a)=0$ by its choice. These are all the required clauses.
